bug_semantics: Authorino's AuthConfig spec.callbacks (originally spec.notify) is an unbounded collection of HTTP endpoints executed concurrently as phase 5 of every auth pipeline, after identity, metadata, authorization, and response. A developer-persona actor who can create or edit an AuthConfig, or a Kuadrant AuthPolicy that compiles into one, can attach arbitrarily many HTTP callbacks. Each Check request then fans out one goroutine and one outbound HTTP call per callback with no CRD maxItems/maxProperties, no controller count cap, and no executor throttle, so a single Authorino instance can be DoS'd while processing post-authorization callbacks (CWE-770/CWE-400).
flaw_origin: The unbounded notify/callback surface was first written in f8895e464ed34300b8aa0e43c410b765c73ff6b4 (PR #368, 2023-01-03) as AuthConfigSpec.Notify []*Notify with no kubebuilder MaxItems, pkg/evaluators/notify.go wrapping GenericHttp, and evaluateNotifyConfigs() driving evaluateAnyAuthConfig (one goroutine per item). Immediate parent 5d1eeea6f0e4cfcfb94fff3cf1fb39b4e1a74565 has no notify/callback types, files, or pipeline phase. Later 1f58b037 only renamed notify to callbacks; v1beta2/v1beta3 conversions kept an unbounded map.

reasoning: Vulnerability-first: CVE-2025-25207 remains PUBLISHED at CVE.org (withdrawn_at on GHSA is null and is not authoritative). The sink is CWE-770 on post-auth HTTP callbacks: AuthConfig.callbacks/notify is an attacker-controlled unbounded collection, and Authorino executes every entry concurrently on each auth request, so a developer-persona AuthPolicy/AuthConfig with a large callback set can exhaust the single Authorino instance. The smallest first-write of that mechanism is f8895e464ed34300b8aa0e43c410b765c73ff6b4, which added the unbounded spec.notify slice, the notify evaluator, and evaluateNotifyConfigs/evaluateAnyAuthConfig fan-out. Parent 5d1eeea6f0e4cfcfb94fff3cf1fb39b4e1a74565 was checked directly and lacks those types/files/phase, so introducer_parent_absent is false. PR #368 is not a squash (feature commit plus docs commit, then merge); 1f58b037 is a rename and is not the BIC. The BIC precedes first affected tag v0.12.0 and is in the GHSA window through v0.20.0; no later tag/HEAD commit adds a count cap, so there is no fix_sha. AI judgment is BIC-object-only: author and committer are Guilherme Cassolato with no AI trailers, so the verdict is NOT_AI on a real unpatched vulnerability.

potential_fix.approach: Add a CRD/admission cap (kubebuilder MaxProperties on spec.callbacks, and MaxItems if any list form remains) plus the same hard limit in the AuthConfig controller and executeCallbacks path so post-auth HTTP fan-out cannot exceed a small bound; optionally run remaining callbacks through a bounded worker pool rather than one goroutine per callback.
potential_fix.rationale: The DoS is allocation of goroutines and outbound HTTP without limits on an attacker-controlled callback map executed on every auth request. Bounding the collection at the API and the executor closes the CWE-770 sink even when a developer-persona AuthPolicy compiles into AuthConfig.
